issue: The orange leader line for the annotation 'generated (γ=65/turn)' does not visibly anchor to the generated segment, because at the 0–14000 token scale a 65-token slice is only ~1.5 px tall (sub-visual). The line floats at the top of the stack, so a reader cannot tell whether it marks the per-turn 65-token increment, the cumulative T·γ, or simply the top of the bar; the only truly invisible component (generated) is the one with the ambiguous callout.
evidence: Panel (a) y-axis 0–14000 over ~330 px plot height ⇒ 1 token ≈ 0.024 px; 65 tokens ≈ 1.5 px. Annotation text 'generated γ=65/turn' with a horizontal orange leader line ending near the top of bars 3–4. Legend lists 'generated (γ=65)' as an orange-hatched swatch that is not resolvable in the bars.
acceptance_test: A reader must be able to locate/size the generated component without the legend: add a per-bar numeric tick for the generated slice, a small zoomed inset, or remove the ambiguous leader and add a note that the γ=65/turn component is below visual resolution at this scale (relying on the legend + the formula in Fig 19.3).

figure: FIGURE 19.3 (Turn 4: three state-management policies) — formula note; and the L_T equation in section 19.5
issue: The formula printed under Figure 19.3 for the append-only total omits the initial-context term, so as printed it does not evaluate to the plotted 34.0 GB; the same formula is written a second, differently-broken way in the prose on printed p. 306.
evidence: Figure 19.3 note: 'append-only total = L4 = T*S + T*Y + O_final @ 2.62 MB/token'. With T=4, S=800, Y=65, O_final=300 this gives 3,760 tokens = 9.9 GB, not the 12,960 tokens / 34.0 GB plotted and labelled. The correct form is L_T = L0 + T*S + T*Y + O_final = 9,200 + 800T + 65T + 300 (T=4 -> 12,960 -> 33.96 GB ~ 34.0 GB). The prose on printed p. 306 prints 'L_T = T*S + T*Y + O_final = 9,200 + 800*T + 65*T = 300', which (i) equates a sum that omits 9,200 with a sum that includes it, and (ii) ends in '= 300' where '+ 300' is required. Figure 19.2's legend already uses the correct symbol for the initial context ('initial context (L0)'), so the book's own notation is available.
acceptance_test: Print the formula in both places as L_T = L0 + T*S + T*Y + O_final = 9,200 + 800T + 65T + 300, and verify by substitution that T=0 -> 9,500 tokens -> 24.9 GB and T=4 -> 12,960 tokens -> 34.0 GB, matching the labels in Figures 19.2 and 19.3 exactly.

issue: The compaction bar is drawn terminating exactly on the 'single-shot 24.9 GB' reference line and labelled with an equals sign, which asserts an exact equality that the caption's own wording ('holds the footprint roughly flat') and the ILLUSTRATIVE status do not support.
evidence: The green bar's right edge coincides with the dashed 'single-shot 24.9 GB' line and carries the label '= 24.9 GB'. The caption states 'compaction (summarize or truncate accumulated history each turn) holds the footprint roughly flat', and the figure's own annotation labels the bar '[ILLUSTRATIVE] summarize/truncate each turn — moves the footprint'. A compaction policy that summarizes each turn still retains the current turn's context plus a summary, so exact equality with the single-shot footprint is not implied.
acceptance_test: Either draw the compaction bar slightly below the 24.9 GB reference line and label it '~ 24.9 GB (illustrative)', or keep the coincidence and change the label to '~ 24.9 GB' with the caption changed to 'returns the footprint to approximately the single-shot level'. The label and the caption must agree on exact vs approximate.

issue: The three value labels are set on top of, or hard against, the right ends of their bars, and the compaction label is green text over a green hatched bar.
evidence: '34.0 GB' (red) sits over the right end of the red dotted bar; '= 24.9 GB' (green) sits over the right end of the green diagonally-hatched bar; '34.0 GB unchanged' (blue) abuts the right end of the blue cross-hatched bar. In grayscale the green-on-green-hatch case loses the glyph edges entirely.
acceptance_test: Place all three value labels outside the bar ends with >= 3 pt clearance from the bar boundary, or place them inside the bars in white with a solid (non-hatched) backing. Verify each label remains readable when the page is converted to grayscale.

issue: The parenthetical '(L4 = 9.2K input, S = 800 retrieved, Y = 65 generated, O_final = 300 output) (once)' mislabels the initial context as L4, which the figure itself defines as the four-turn total.
evidence: The note reads 'L4 = 9.2K input' while the line above defines 'append-only total = L4'. The 9.2K figure is the initial context, which Figure 19.2's legend calls L0.
acceptance_test: Change to '(L0 = 9.2K input, S = 800 retrieved, Y = 65 generated, O_final = 300 output) (once)' and confirm the symbol L0 is used consistently with Figure 19.2's legend.

issue: The label 'actually-served demand region' sits in the empty area below the dotted S line, not on the line, and the word 'region' may imply the area under the line represents served demand. The served demand is the line S = min(40, C_eff), not the area.
evidence: Label at approximately x=35, y=20; dotted S line at y=40; legend defines S as a line.
acceptance_test: Move the label to the dotted S line or change it to 'S = actually-served demand (line)' and remove 'region'.

issue: The caption instructs the reader to 'Read the two bars', but the figure is a three-curve line chart with no bars; the caption also refers to 'this two-line calculation' two sentences later, so the caption contradicts itself about the figure's geometry.
evidence: Caption: 'Reading the two bars: below saturation the -5% gap between C_analytic and C_eff is the assumed throughput-efficiency derate; above saturation C_eff - S is unused capacity from insufficient offered demand, not scheduling overhead (demand is capped at 40 rps). Queuing/tail-latency penalties are not determined by this two-line calculation and must be shown separately.' The figure contains three lines (solid C_analytic, dashed C_eff, dotted S) and one shaded region.
acceptance_test: Replace 'the two bars' with 'the two capacity curves' (or 'the three curves'), and make the later reference consistent ('this three-curve construction'). Confirm the caption's description matches the drawn mark types exactly.

issue: The caption presents '21/22-host planning sizing' as the planning answer, but the adjacent text on printed p. 320 states that the fleet must satisfy four requirements — 21, 22, 23 and 32 hosts — with 32 the largest. A reader who takes the figure's caption at face value will under-size the fleet.
evidence: Figure 20.1 caption: '...the 21/22-host planning sizing — 21 ideal / 22 at 95% efficiency — a plateau at the workload's demand ceiling'. In-figure annotation: '21 hosts (ideal) / 22 at 95%: served demand plateaus at 40 rps'. The prose immediately preceding the figure (printed p. 320) says: 'The correct statement is: the fleet must satisfy four requirements — 21 hosts under case (i), 22 hosts under case (ii), with the standard p = 0.95 derate applied to the prefill screen ... case (i) rises to [21.8/0.95] = 23 hosts ... and that the 70% SLO is the prefill screen ... case (ii) is [21.8/0.66] = 32 ... all of 19/21/22/23/32 are illustrative planning scenarios'. The figure models only the throughput/KV-residency screen (17 contexts @ 8.6 s per host) and omits the prefill screen that the prose identifies as binding.
acceptance_test: Rewrite the caption so the figure's scope is explicit, e.g. 'this figure models the throughput/KV-residency screen only (21 hosts ideal, 22 at 95% efficiency); the prefill screen in Sec. 20.24.1 requires 23 hosts (case i) to 32 hosts (case ii) and is the binding requirement'. Confirm no sentence in the caption or the in-figure annotation presents 21/22 as the fleet size.

figure: FIGURE 20.1, vertical reference lines at N = 21 and N = 22
issue: The two vertical dotted reference lines are one host apart on a 0–60 axis, i.e. roughly 5 pt of separation at print size, and are drawn in the same style, so the reader cannot tell which line is 21 and which is 22.
evidence: The annotation '21 hosts (ideal) / 22 at 95%: served demand plateaus at 40 rps' points at two closely spaced vertical dotted lines near x = 21–22. The knee of the dotted 'actually-served demand' curve is at N = 40/(0.95 x 17/8.6) = 21.3, i.e. between the two lines, so neither line coincides with the visible flattening point.
acceptance_test: Label the two lines directly ('N=21' and 'N=22') with leader text placed at different heights, or use distinct line styles (solid vs dashed) for the two references, and add a marker at the actual knee (N = 21.3). Verify the two references are individually identifiable at 100% print size.

figure: FIGURE 20.1, 'canonical peak = 40 rps' label and dotted line styles
issue: The 'canonical peak = 40 rps' label is set directly on the horizontal dotted reference line, and that line shares its dotted style with the 'actually-served demand' curve, so the two are hard to tell apart where they coincide at the plateau.
evidence: The label 'canonical peak = 40 rps' sits on the y = 40 dotted line at the left of the plot; the legend's third entry 'actually-served demand S = min(40, C_eff) (req/s)' is also a dotted blue line, and the two overlap exactly for N > 21.3.
acceptance_test: Offset the 'canonical peak = 40 rps' label above the line (or add a white halo) and give the horizontal reference a distinct style (e.g. dash-dot) from the S curve. Confirm the reader can trace each of the three curves from the legend to the plateau.

issue: The annotation expresses the derate as '(1-5%)', which is not a well-defined multiplicative factor and reads as a subtraction of 5 percentage points rather than a 5% reduction in capacity.
evidence: In-figure text: 'throughput-efficiency derate = (1-5%) -> C_eff = 0.95 x C_analytic'. The legend states the same thing correctly as 'C_eff = 0.95 x C_analytic (req/s)'.
acceptance_test: Rewrite as 'throughput-efficiency derate: x0.95 -> C_eff = 0.95 x C_analytic' so the annotation and the legend express the factor identically.

issue: Internal semantic mismatch inside the figure: the in-figure summary line claims the gates check 'measured throughput / SLO / cost', but no gate in the drawn diagram checks throughput.
evidence: The six gate boxes are labeled: Data 'src valid', Train 'cost ok', Eval 'qual ok', Canary 'health ok', Observe 'TTFT ok', Promote 'cost ok'. The bold in-figure footer directly below the rollback bar reads 'Gates check measured throughput / SLO / cost; a breach rolls back.' 'measured throughput' corresponds to none of the six drawn gate criteria (TTFT/health map to SLO; two gates map to cost; src/qual map to neither). A reader comparing footer to gates sees a promised check that the diagram does not contain. Stage count and gate count are otherwise correct (7 stages, 6 gates, 6 FAIL branches to the rollback bar, matching the caption).
acceptance_test: Either add a throughput criterion to a drawn gate (e.g. Observe: 'throughput ok') or revise the in-figure footer to the criteria actually drawn (e.g. 'Gates check data quality / SLO / cost; a breach rolls back.'); confirm footer terms map 1:1 onto the six gate sub-labels.

issue: The bottom gray summary line 'Gates check measured throughput / SLO / cost' does not match the six drawn gate labels (Data: src valid; Train: cost ok; Eval: qual ok; Canary: health ok; Observe: TTFT ok; Promote: cost ok). 'throughput' appears as no gate, while the quality and health gates are absent from the summary, so the figure's own text and its own boxes disagree on what the gates measure.
evidence: Red box labels read 'src valid / cost ok / qual ok / health ok / TTFT ok / cost ok'; the gray line beneath the green loop reads 'Gates check measured throughput / SLO / cost; a breach rolls back.'
acceptance_test: Rewrite the bottom line to enumerate the actual gate dimensions (e.g., data validity / cost / quality / health / SLO) or add a throughput gate to the top row so the summary and the six drawn gates are consistent.

issue: Red is used both for the PASS gate boxes/checkmarks and for the FAIL bar. The color semantics do not distinguish success from failure; a reader scanning color alone sees red on both paths.
evidence: Six gate boxes have red borders, red 'PASS' text, and red checkmarks; the failure bar is dark red and labeled 'FAIL'. The caption says 'PASS permits the next stage; each labeled FAIL branch...' The labels distinguish, but the color does not.
acceptance_test: Use a non-red treatment for PASS gates (e.g., neutral/blue/green) and reserve red for the FAIL path, or make the gate boxes neutral and color only the PASS/FAIL status indicators.

figure: FIGURE 22.1 (AI Factory lifecycle) vs FIGURE 22.1 (prefill FLOP crossover)
issue: Two different figures in the book carry the identical number 22.1. PDF p.353 (printed 333, chapter 'The AI Factory') is captioned 'FIGURE 22.1: The model-lifecycle layer runs Data -> Train -> Eval -> Canary -> Observe -> Promote -> Serve.' PDF p.361 (printed 341, chapter 'How to Think Like an AI Solution Architect') is captioned 'FIGURE 22.1: Attention vs. projection prefill FLOP crossover.' The surrounding numbering scheme is chapter-scoped and otherwise unique (23.1 on printed 352, 24.1 on printed 364, 24.4.1 on printed 364, 26.1 on printed 383), so one of the two labels is wrong.
evidence: Printed 333: 'FIGURE 22.1: The model-lifecycle layer runs Data -> Train -> Eval -> Canary -> Observe -> Promote -> Serve.' Printed 341: 'FIGURE 22.1: Attention vs. projection prefill FLOP crossover.' Printed 340: 'Note 22.1-1 (Fig 22.1) - crossover derivation' and printed 341 caption 'Derivation: Note 22.1-1 below.' The note number 22.1-1 and the note's own placement inside the 'How to Think' chapter indicate that chapter 22 owns the crossover figure; the AI Factory figure therefore carries a stale/incorrect number.
acceptance_test: Exactly one figure in the book bears the number 22.1. Renumber the AI Factory figure to its correct chapter-scoped number (e.g. 21.x) and update every in-text, caption, note, and cross-reference that points to it; then re-run the figure-number uniqueness and reference-resolution gates over the whole book.

figure: FIGURE 22.1 (AI Factory lifecycle), green feedback arrow
issue: The caption says 'Production feedback returns evidence to data/evaluation, where the gates apply again', but the drawn green feedback arrow terminates only on the Data box; nothing in the drawing routes evidence to Eval. The caption promises two destinations; the figure shows one.
evidence: Printed 333: green arrow runs from the Serve end of the pipeline back along the top and drops into 'Data'; caption 'Production feedback returns evidence to data/evaluation, where the gates apply again.'
acceptance_test: Either split the feedback arrow so it lands on both Data and Eval, or change the caption to 'returns evidence to data'. The caption and the drawn arrow must name the same set of destinations.

issue: The annotation under the gate row says 'gates check measured throughput / SLO / cost; a breach rolls back', but no gate in the figure checks throughput: the six gates read 'Data src valid', 'Train cost ok', 'Eval qual ok', 'Canary health ok', 'Observe TTFT ok', 'Promote cost ok'. Throughput is neither checked nor mentioned, and 'src valid' and 'qual ok' are not throughput/SLO/cost either.
evidence: Printed 333 figure: gate boxes 'Data src valid / PASS', 'Train cost ok / PASS', 'Eval qual ok / PASS', 'Canary health ok / PASS', 'Observe TTFT ok / PASS', 'Promote cost ok / PASS'; annotation 'gates check measured throughput / SLO / cost; a breach rolls back'.
acceptance_test: Make the annotation enumerate the metrics actually gated (e.g. 'gates check data validity, training cost, eval quality, canary health, TTFT, and promotion cost'), or add a throughput gate to the drawing. The annotation and the six gate labels must enumerate the same set.

issue: The 'Serve' box is drawn with a diagonal hatch while every other stage is solid, but neither the figure nor the caption explains what the hatch encodes. The reader can infer 'not gated' from the caption's 'Six-box FAIL decision', but the encoding is left to inference, and in grayscale the hatch is the only thing distinguishing Serve from the other stages.
evidence: Printed 333: 'Serve' box rendered with diagonal hatching; caption mentions only 'Six-box FAIL decision on a measured metric, not a hand-off' and never mentions the hatch.
acceptance_test: Add a short legend or caption clause, e.g. 'hatched = not gated (Serve)', so the visual encoding is stated rather than inferred.
